site.title: Somehow I Managed — Field notes from 21 years running hotels | Alejandro Soria
site.description: A free hotel operations book by Alejandro Soria, a multi-brand general manager. Six field notes on reading the building, leading people, and running the business behind the work. Read or listen free.

hero.eyebrow: Field notes from 21 years running hotels
hero.headline: The building always knows first.
hero.headlineAccent: This book teaches you to hear it.
hero.sub: Somehow I Managed is the hotel operations book I wish someone had handed me on day one. Six lessons from a multi-brand general manager who has run hotels, fixed them, and opened one from the ground up.

author.name: Alejandro Soria
author.role: Multi-brand general manager and hospitality operator
bio: Alejandro has spent 21 years in hotels: full-service, select-service and extended-stay, across several major brands. He has turned properties around, led teams through storms and sold-out weekends, and opened a hotel from the ground up.
He writes about the work the way it actually happens: the building, the people, and the business plan behind both. These field notes are updated as he goes.

quiz.title: What kind of operator are you?
quiz.sub: Six quick questions. Find your instinct, and the chapter that will stretch you.

questions.q: Your first week at a new hotel. Where do you start?

options.text: Walk every floor, closet and mechanical room
Sit down one-on-one with every department lead
Read the P&L and the owner's plan for the asset
Map the problems that keep coming back

questions.q: A guest is furious at the front desk. What do you do first?

options.text: Listen. Human first, facts second
Stand beside your agent, coach them later
Find the process that failed this guest
Check what we promised at booking

questions.q: Labor ran over plan last week. Your first question?

options.text: Did pickup beat the forecast?
What did the floor look like those days?
Is the schedule built from habit or from demand?
Is the team running on empty?
The same problem returning every week
Meetings full of information and empty of decisions
People who won't tell me the truth
Nobody seeing the whole picture

questions.q: Your best day at work looks like...

options.text: A manager makes the call without phoning me
The numbers close exactly where they should
A new hire finally gets it
A storm hits and the team stays calm

s01.name: The Floor Reader
s01.line: You trust what you see over what the report says. You walk first and ask why.

s02.name: The People Builder
s02.line: You know nothing moves without people, and you build teams that tell you the truth.

s03.name: The Numbers Translator
s03.line: You see the hotel as an economic model and connect the floor to the P&L.

s04.name: The System Fixer
s04.line: You get tired of solving the same problem twice, so you fix what keeps causing it.

s05.name: The Pressure Holder
s05.line: You absorb complexity and return clarity. The team gets calmer when you walk in.

s06.name: The Long-Game Operator
s06.line: You build an operation that runs without you, and you still enjoy the ride.
